title: FATHER GOD, GIVE ME REST FROM EVERY BATTLE OF TODAY | APOSTLE JOSHUA SELMAN
paragraphs: Glory to God in the highest. I want you to lift up your voice right now wherever you are and say, "Father, I receive rest." Say it again with authority, "I receive rest." One more time, say it like you mean it. I receive divine rest from every battle of today. You know, beloved, when we come into the presence of the almighty, we don't come with mere religiosity. We come with understanding that there is a dimension of grace available to the sons and daughters of Zion that transcends human comprehension.

The Bible says in Matthew chapter 11 verse 28, and Jesus himself spoke these words. He said, "Come on to me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest." This is not just a suggestion. This is an invitation from the throne room of heaven into a place of supernatural quietness in the midst of storms. Now, I want to establish something from the very foundation of scripture.

When God finished creating the heavens and the earth, the Bible records in Genesis chapter 2 verse 2 that he rested on the seventh day. But you must understand something. God did not rest because he was tired. Isaiah chapter 40 verse 28 tells us that the everlasting God, the Lord, the creator of the ends of the earth, fainted not, neither is weary. So, if God doesn't get tired, why did he rest?

He rested to establish a pattern, to demonstrate a principle that rest is not the absence of work, but rest is the presence of completion. Rest is the presence of divine order. Rest is the presence of finished works. And so today, or wherever this word meets you, I stand in the office of a prophet to declare that there are battles you have been fighting that God says are already finished. There are struggles you have been engaging with that the blood of Jesus has already concluded.

There are warfare assignments that have been terrorizing your destiny that the resurrection power of Christ has already terminated. And so we are not praying to start a new battle. We are praying to enforce what heaven has already concluded. Let me take you to the book of Exodus. When the children of Israel came to the Red Sea, they found themselves in what I call a strategic position of impossibility. Behind them was Pharaoh and his army. Before them was the Red Sea. To their left and right were mountains.

In the natural, they were trapped. In the natural, they were finished. In the natural, their destiny was about to be aborted. But in Exodus chapter 14 verse 13, Moses said something powerful. He said, "Fear ye not. Stand still and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will show to you today. For the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you shall see them again no more forever." And then in verse 14, he made a declaration that I want you to write in the tablets of your heart.

He said, "The Lord shall fight for you, and you shall hold your peace." Do you know what it means to hold your peace? It means to enter into rest. It means to cease from your own struggling. It means to stop operating in the energy of the flesh and begin to align with the finished works of Calvary. You see, there is a warfare that belongs to man, and there is a warfare that belongs to God.

There is a dimension of battle where you must put on the whole armor of God and stand, but there is also a dimension where you must simply rest in the victory that has already been won. I prophesy over your life right now. Every battle that you were not ordained to fight, I command it to cease in the name of Jesus. Every warfare that is above your grade and your grace, I declare that the captain of the host takes over right now in the mighty name of Jesus.

Every assignment of hell that has been draining your energy, exhausting your strength, and stealing your peace, I command a divine interruption in the name that is above every other name. Now, let us go to the New Testament. In the book of Hebrews chapter 4, beginning from verse 1, the scripture says, "Let us therefore fear, lest a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it." Now, watch verse 3. "For we which have believed do enter into rest." Did you see that?

It is believers that enter into rest. It is not fighters who enter into rest. It is believers. Your faith is the key that unlocks the door of divine rest. You see, many believers are exhausted today, not because the battle is too strong, but because they have not understood the finished works of Jesus Christ. When Jesus was on the cross, just before he gave up the ghost, he said three words that changed the entire spiritual climate of humanity. He said, "It is finished." Not it will be finished.

Not it might be finished, but it is finished. Tetelestai in the Greek language, paid in full, completed, accomplished, done. What was finished? Every battle that would ever rise against the seed of Abraham was finished. Every curse that would ever attempt to limit your potential was broken. Every demon that would ever try to harass your destiny was defeated. Every sickness that would ever try to cut short your lifespan was destroyed. Every poverty spirit that would ever try to cage your prosperity was paralyzed.

It is finished. And so when you come into prayer today, you are not coming to beg God to do something new. You are coming to enforce what has already been done. You are coming to apply the blood. You are coming to activate the resurrection power. You are coming to declare that because Jesus won, you win. Because he overcame, you overcome. Because he triumphed, you triumph. Let me show you something in the book of Joshua.

After Moses died, God spoke to Joshua and said in chapter 1 verse 3, "Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you, as I said unto Moses." Now, this is critical. God said, "I have given." Past tense. Before Joshua ever stepped into the land, God said it was already given. The battle was already won in the spirit before it was ever fought in the natural. And so God is saying to somebody here today, that business is already given. That contract is already released.

That marriage is already settled. That healing is already done. That breakthrough is already manifest in the realm of the spirit. Now, all you need to do is step into your possession. All you need to do is enter into your rest and receive what grace has already provided. But the enemy knows that if you ever discover the power of rest, his entire strategy will collapse. And so he keeps you busy. He keeps you anxious. He keeps you worried. He keeps you fearful.

He keeps you fighting battles that were already concluded 2,000 years ago on a hill called Calvary. The devil is a liar. And today, we serve him an eviction notice from your peace, from your rest, from your joy, from your calmness in the name of Jesus Christ. I want you to go with me to the book of Psalms.

David, a man after God's own heart, a man who fought many battles, a man who faced Goliath, a man who ran from Saul, a man who dealt with his own children rebelling against him, this same David wrote in Psalm 23, one of the most powerful chapters in scripture. He said, "The Lord is my shepherd. I shall not want." Now, when you say "I shall not want," you are making a declaration of rest. You are saying I am not in lack. I am not in need. I am not in anxiety." And then he goes further.

"He maketh me to lie down in green pastures. He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul." Do you see the picture? God is leading you to a place of stillness. He's leading you to a place of restoration. He's leading you to a place where the battles cannot reach you because you are hidden in him. And then David says something that shakes the kingdom of darkness. "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for thou art with me."

Notice, he didn't say, "I will run through the valley." He said, "I will walk." Walking is a posture of rest. Walking is a posture of confidence. Walking is a posture that says, "I know my God is with me, and if God is with me, who can be against me?" And then, beloved, listen to this. He said, "Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies." What kind of God prepares a feast in the middle of warfare? What kind of God sets a table while demons are watching?

What kind of God gives you rest while the battle is still raging around you? Only the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Only the God who makes a way where there is no way. Only the God who gives PEACE THAT PASSES ALL UNDERSTANDING. I prophesy to somebody in the presence of that enemy, in the presence of that affliction, in the presence of that attack, God is about to prepare a table for you. While they are expecting you to collapse, you will be feasting.

While they are expecting you to break down, you will be celebrating. While they are expecting you to surrender, you will be declaring victory in the name of Jesus. Now, let me take you into a deeper dimension. The Bible says in Philippians chapter 4 verse 6 and 7, "Be careful for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."

Do Do see that word keep? It is a military term. It means to guard. It means to garrison. It means to mount a protective fence around something precious. God is saying that when you enter into prayer with Thanksgiving, when you make your request known onto him, he releases a dimension of peace that the human mind cannot comprehend. And this peace acts as a soldier, as a guard, as a fortress around your heart and your mind.

So, even when the battle is raging, even when the enemy is shouting, even when circumstances are screaming, your heart remains at rest because it is fortified by divine peace. This is not the peace the world gives. Jesus said in John chapter 14 verse 27, "Peace I leave with you. My peace I give unto you. Not as the world giveth give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid." The world's peace is conditional, it depends on circumstances.

But the peace of God is unconditional, it transcends circumstances. The world's peace says when everything is calm, then I will be calm. But God's peace says even in the storm, I am still. Even in the fire, I am cool. Even in the battle, I am at rest. Let me tell you about three Hebrew boys, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They were thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter than usual, but something miraculous happened.

When the king looked into the fire, he saw four men walking and the form of the fourth was like the son of God. They were in the fire, but the fire was not in them. They were in the battle, but the battle was not in them. They were in the crisis, but the crisis was not in them. This is the rest of God and I decree over your life you will go through, but it will not go through you. You will pass through the fire, but you will not be burned. You will walk through the flood, but you will not be drowned.

Isaiah 43:2, "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee. And through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee. When thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned, neither shall the flame kindle upon thee." Now, somebody needs to understand something today. Rest is not laziness. Rest is not inactivity. Rest is not complacency. Biblical rest is the position of a believer who has done everything and now stands in faith watching God perform his word.

Ephesians chapter 6 tells us to put on the whole armor of God to stand against the wiles of the devil and having done all to stand. That standing is a position of rest. When you stand in faith, you are saying, "God, I have prayed. I have declared your word. I have activated my faith. Now I rest in your faithfulness. I rest in your promises. I rest in your covenant. I rest in your ability to perform what you have spoken." This is the rest that gives God room to work.

Because when you are anxious, you are operating in unbelief. When you are worried, you are doubting God's power. But when you rest, you are expressing absolute confidence in the one who cannot fail. Let me take you to the book of 2 Chronicles chapter 20. Jehoshaphat and the children of Judah were surrounded by three enemy nations. The situation was impossible in the natural, but Jehoshaphat did something powerful. He proclaimed a fast and inquired of the Lord.

And God spoke to a prophet and said in verse 15, "Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God's." And then in verse 17, God said something that would transform your prayer life. He said, "Ye shall not need to fight in this battle. Set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the Lord with you, oh Judah and Jerusalem. Fear not nor be dismayed. Tomorrow go out against them, for the Lord will be with you." Did you hear that?

You shall not need to fight. God is saying, "Just show up. Just stand still. Just watch me work." And what did they do? Verse 21 says that Jehoshaphat appointed singers to go before the army praising the beauty of holiness and saying, "Praise the Lord, for his mercy endureth forever." Can you imagine? In the face of warfare, they were worshiping. In the face of death, they were praising. In the face of impossibility, they were magnifying God.

And as they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushments against their enemies and they destroyed one another. The battle was won without Judah lifting a sword. This is the power of rest. This is the victory of worship. This is what happens when you refuse to panic and instead choose to praise. And I decree over your life, as you worship God today, as you magnify his name, as you exalt him above your circumstances, God is setting ambushments against every enemy that has risen against you.

Confusion will enter the camp of your adversaries. They will fight against themselves. They will destroy one another and you will emerge victorious without a scar. In the name of Jesus. Now, let me address something Some of you are wondering, "Man of God, I've been praying, but the battle is not ending." "I have been fasting, but the situation is not changing. I have been standing, but the breakthrough is not coming."

Let me tell you what the Holy Spirit is saying, "Your breakthrough is not delayed, it is being prepared. Your miracle is not denied, it is being packaged. Your victory is not canceled, it is being processed." You see, there is a difference between God's timing and your expectation. Isaiah chapter 55:8 says, "For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord."

Sometimes God allows the battle to linger, not because he's weak, but because he's preparing you for a greater dimension of glory. Sometimes he allows the pressure to increase, not because he has forgotten you, but because he's positioning you for a testimony that will shake nations. Think about Joseph. He had a dream, but between the dream and the manifestation were 13 years of battles, slavery, false accusation, prison, but every battle was strategically preparing him for the palace.

Every test was developing the character he needed to handle the throne. And when his time came, he went from prison to prime minister in one day, from the dungeon to the palace in 24 hours. This is the God we serve. And I prophesy to somebody, your suddenly is coming. Your speedily is approaching. Your quickly is at the door. Everything that has been delayed will be accelerated. Everything that has been postponed will be fast-tracked.

Everything that has been held back will be released in a flood in the mighty name of Jesus. But until then, rest. Until then, trust. Until then, believe. Because he who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ. Let me pray with you now. And I want you to engage your spirit. This is not a casual prayer. This is a militant declaration. Lift up your voice wherever you are and begin to pray.

Father, in the name of Jesus, I come before your throne of grace with boldness, not because of my righteousness, but because of the blood of Jesus that has made me righteous. I thank you, Lord, that I'm not approaching you as a beggar, but as a son, as a daughter, as an heir of God and joint heir with Christ. Father, your word declares in Psalm 68:1, "Let God arise. Let his enemies be scattered." And so I declare right now, let God arise in my life. Let God arise in my family. Let God arise in my finances.

Let God arise in my health. Let God arise in my destiny. And as you arise, oh Lord, let every enemy of my rest be scattered in the name of Jesus. I speak to every battle that is raging against my peace. Right now, be still in the name of Jesus. I command every storm that is threatening my tranquility, be calm in the name of Jesus. I decree to every warfare that is stealing my joy, be terminated in the name of Jesus. For the Lord has said, "The battle is not yours, but God's."

And so I release this battle into your hands, Father, and I step into the rest that you have provided for me. Every spirit of anxiety that has been assigned against my mind, I bind you and I cast you out in the name of Jesus. Every demon of worry that has been stealing my sleep, I command you to lose your hold and depart in the name of Jesus. Every force of fear that has been manipulating my emotions, I rebuke you by the authority of the word of God.

For God has not given me a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind. Father, I receive your peace that passes all understanding. I receive your rest that transcends human comprehension. I receive your calmness that defies natural explanation. And I decree that my heart will not be troubled, neither will it be afraid because you are with me, you are for me, and you are in me. Every battle that I was not ordained to fight, I release it right now in the name of Jesus.

Every warfare that is above my capacity, I surrender it into your mighty hands, oh God. For you are the Lord of hosts, the captain of the armies of heaven, the commander of angel battalions. And when you fight, victory is guaranteed. When you intervene, breakthrough is certain. When you show up, impossibilities bow. I decree that even as I sleep today, angels are warring on my behalf. Even as I rest, the hosts of heaven are fighting for my cause. Even as I am still, the arm of the Lord is moving in my situation.

I will not struggle in the flesh. I will not strive in my own strength. But I will rest in your finished works, oh God. And watch you perform wonders in my life. Father, I thank you because you have prepared a table before me in the presence of my enemies while they watch. I am feasting while they scheme. I am celebrating. While they attack, I am resting in your promises. My cup runs over with your blessings. My head is anointed with the oil of your favor.

And surely goodness and mercy are following me all the days of my life. I speak to every weapon that has been fashioned against me, you shall not prosper in the name of Jesus. I speak to every tongue that has risen against me in judgment. I condemn you by the authority of God's word. For this is my heritage as a servant of the Lord. And my righteousness is from you, oh God. Every battle of today, I command you to end right now in the name of Jesus.

Every struggle of this season, I decree your expiration in the name of Jesus. Every warfare of this moment, I declare your termination in the name of Jesus. For the Lord has said in his word, "Come on to me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest." And I receive that rest right now by faith. Glory to God in the highest. I want you to understand something profound as we continue in this atmosphere of divine rest.

The Bible says in Exodus chapter 33 verse 14, when Moses was concerned about the journey ahead, when he was worried about leading millions of people through the wilderness, God gave him a promise that has echoed through generations. God said, "My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest." Do you see that? Rest is not a location. Rest is a person. Rest is not a circumstance. Rest is a presence. When you have God's presence, you have God's rest.

And so, the question is not whether your circumstances are calm. The question is whether you are carrying the presence of the Almighty. The question is not whether the battle has ended. The question is whether the God of the battle is with you. Because I have discovered something in my walk with God. When his presence is in the room, demons become confused. When his glory fills the atmosphere, situations begin to shift. When his spirit takes over, impossibilities start bowing.

Let me take you to the book of Acts chapter 12. Peter was in prison, bound with chains, guarded by 16 soldiers, sentenced to death. In the natural, his situation was hopeless. But the Bible says in verse five, prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him. And something happened in the realm of the spirit. An angel of the Lord appeared. Light shined in the prison. The chains fell off Peter's hands. The iron gate opened of its own accord. And Peter walked out into freedom.

Now, here is what I want you to see. Peter was so at rest in that prison that when the angel came to deliver him, the Bible says he was sleeping. Sleeping. Not pacing. Not panicking. Not crying. He was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, knowing he was scheduled to die the next day. And he was sleeping. This is the rest that comes from knowing that your life is hidden with Christ in God. This is the peace that comes from understanding that if God be for you, no man can successfully be against you.

Asleep in a storm while water was filling the boat, while the disciples were panicking, while death was threatening, Jesus was sleeping. Why? Because he knew something they didn't know. He knew that he had already spoken the destination. He had said, "Let us pass over onto the other side." He didn't say, "Let us go halfway and drown." He said, "Let us pass over." And if he said it, then it was settled. The storm could rage, but it could not stop the word that had been spoken.

And when the disciples woke him up in their panic, Jesus stood up and spoke three words to the storm, "Peace. Be still." And immediately the wind ceased. And there was a great calm. Now, watch what he said to his disciples. He said, "Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?" He was saying, "You have been with me. You have seen my power. You know my word. Why are you afraid?" And God is asking somebody the same question today, "Why are you afraid? Have I not proven myself faithful?

Have I not delivered you before? Have I not made a way when there was no way? Have I not opened doors that no man could shut? Have I not healed what doctors said was incurable? Have I not provided when provision seemed impossible? Why are you afraid?" I decree over your life, the same Jesus who calmed the storm on the sea of Galilee is in your boat today. The same power that spoke, "Peace. Be still." is available in your situation right now.

And just as the wind and the waves obeyed him, every storm in your life must obey him. Every turbulence in your finances must obey him. Every chaos in your family must obey him. Every confusion in your mind must obey him. Peace. Be still. In the mighty name of Jesus. Let me take you deeper into this mystery of rest. The writer of Hebrews in chapter four verse nine says, "There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God." The word rest here in the Greek is sabbatismos.

It means a Sabbath rest, a ceasing from labor. And then verse 10 says, "For he that is entered into his rest, he also has ceased from his own works as God did from his." Do you see this? When you enter into God's rest, you cease from your own works. You stop trying to make things happen in your own strength. You stop striving in your own ability. You stop struggling in your own wisdom. This is the problem with many believers today. They are working harder than God.

They are more concerned about the situation than the one who controls the situation. They are more focused on the problem than the problem solver. And God is saying, "Cease from your own works. Stop trying to figure it all out. Stop carrying burdens I never asked you to carry. Let me be God in your situation." I remember the story of Mary and Martha in the book of Luke chapter 10. Jesus came to their house. And Martha was busy serving, distracted with much serving, worried and troubled about many things.

But Mary sat at Jesus' feet and heard his word. And when Martha complained, Jesus said something powerful. He said, "Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things, but one thing is needful. And Mary had chosen that good part which shall not be taken away from her." Mary chose rest. She chose presence. She chose to sit and hear rather than stress and serve. And Jesus said that was the good part. I'm not saying don't work. I'm not saying don't serve.

But I'm saying that your intimacy with God must come before your activity for God. Your communion must come before your commission. Your sitting must come before your serving. Because when you are full of his presence, the work becomes effortless. When you are saturated with his peace, the service becomes joyful. When you are established in his rest, the labor becomes light. And I speak to somebody who has been like Martha, stressed, worried, troubled about many things. God is calling you back to the feet of Jesus.

He's calling you back to the place of rest. He's calling you back to the place where you simply sit and receive. Stop striving. Stop struggling. Stop stressing. And simply sit at his feet and let him fill you with his peace. Now, as we begin to close this word, I want to give you practical keys to walking in divine rest. First, you must renew your mind with the word of God. Romans chapter 12 verse two says, "Be not conformed to this world, but be you transformed by the renewing of your mind."

Your mind is the battlefield. If the enemy can control your thoughts, he can control your life. But when you fill your mind with God's promises, when you meditate on his word day and night, when you speak his truth over your situation, your mind becomes a fortress of peace. Second, you must practice the presence of God. Brother Lawrence wrote about practicing the presence of God in every moment, whether washing dishes, walking, working, or resting.

When you become conscious that God is with you always, that he never leaves you nor forsakes you, that his eyes are always upon you, fear loses its grip, anxiety loses its power, worry loses its control because you realize you are never alone. You are never abandoned. You are never forsaken. Third, you must develop a lifestyle of worship and thanksgiving. The Bible says in 1 Thessalonians chapter five verse 18, "In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you."

When you worship in the midst of your battle, you are declaring that God is bigger than your problem. When you give thanks in your trial, you are affirming that God is working all things for your good. Worship shifts the atmosphere. Thanksgiving changes your perspective. Praise prepares you for victory. I decree that you are entering a new season, a season where rest is your portion, a season where peace is your inheritance, a season where joy is your strength.

The battle may be raging around you, but in you there is perfect calm. The storm may be threatening, but in you there is supernatural stillness. The enemy may be shouting, but in you there is divine silence that speaks louder than any attack. Go forth today knowing that you are more than a conqueror through him who loved you. Go forth knowing that no weapon formed against you shall prosper. Go forth knowing that the Lord your God is with you, mighty to save, and he will rejoice over you with singing.

You are blessed beyond measure. You are favored beyond comprehension. Father, I thank you because the victory is already won. The battle is already finished. The breakthrough is already secured, and I stand on the finished works of Calvary declaring that it is well with my soul, it is well with my family, it is well with my destiny, it is well with my future in the mighty name of Jesus Christ. Now, beloved, as you continue from this moment, I want you to operate in a new consciousness. You are not a victim.

You are a victor. You are not defeated. You are triumphant. You are not under attack. You are under grace. The battle may be around you, but it is not in you. The warfare may be visible, but victory is inevitable. I decree and I declare that from this moment forward, you will walk in supernatural rest. Your mind will be stayed on God, and he will keep you in perfect peace. Your heart will trust in his promises, and you will not be shaken. Your faith will anchor in his faithfulness, and you will not be moved.

Every sleepless night is over in the name of Jesus. Every anxious thought is bound in the name of Jesus. Every fearful imagination is cast down in the name of Jesus. You will rest. You will sleep. You will be calm. You will be still, and you will see the salvation of the Lord manifesting in every area of your life. I see you walking in victory. I see you operating in peace. I see you functioning in joy. I see you carrying the presence of God with such weight that battles dissolve in your presence.

I see you so secure in God's love that the enemy's threats sound like whispers of defeat. I see you so established in faith that mountains move at your word. This is your season of divine rest. This is your moment of supernatural peace. This is your time of heavenly calmness, and no weapon formed against it shall prosper. No enemy assigned against it shall succeed. No demon orchestrated against it shall prevail. For the Lord God omnipotent reigns, and his rest is your portion in Jesus' mighty name.

Now, go in peace. Walk in victory. Live in rest, and let the world see that you serve a God who gives rest in the midst of battles, peace in the midst of storms, and joy in the midst of challenges. You are blessed. You are favored. You are victorious in Jesus' mighty name. Amen.
